verdicts.back_translation: For any type R with a commutative ring structure, any natural number n, and any family I of ideals of R indexed by Fin n, if every two distinct indexed ideals have supremum equal to the top ideal, then the infimum over all indexed ideals equals their finite product.

conclusion_matches.note: The Lean conclusion states that the indexed infimum of the ideals, i.e. their intersection, equals the finite product of the same indexed family.

hypothesis_completeness.note: The Lean statement includes a commutative ring R, a finite family of ideals indexed by n, and pairwise comaximality. The all-distinct index condition is equivalent to the paper's i < j formulation for this symmetric ideal-supremum condition.

issues.message: The Lean statement indexes the family by Fin n rather than by 1 through n; this is a standard reindexing and does not change the mathematical content.

verdicts.paper_text: Let R be a commutative ring and let I_1, ..., I_n be ideals of R that are pairwise comaximal, i.e. I_i + I_j = R for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n. Then the intersection of the ideals equals their product: the intersection over i from 1 to n of I_i equals the product over i from 1 to n of I_i.

verdicts.back_translation: For all natural numbers d_1 and d_2, if d_1 is not equal to d_2, then the Laurent-polynomial images of (cyclotomic d_1 over Q) composed with X^2 and (cyclotomic d_2 over Q) composed with X^2 are coprime, and the supremum of the two principal ideals generated by those Laurent polynomials is the top ideal.

hypothesis_completeness.note: The paper hypothesis d_1 != d_2 appears directly as the Lean assumption h : d_1 != d_2, with d_1 and d_2 bound as natural numbers.
